name: Kank
sum: Medium-sized unenlagiid from the Maastrichtian Chorrillo Formation of Patagonia, Argentina, the first of its family recorded there, known from fragments.
wsnote: Bones are similar in size to those of Neuquenraptor (Wikipedia revision 1380974870); no estimate for Kank itself.
holotype: MPM-PV-23106-A, a single vertebra from the 'Monotreme site', Chorrillo Formation, Santa Cruz, Argentina.
material: Three pedal phalanges and five teeth from the same spot; other fragments from the formation may belong to it.
biology: The small teeth are curved and unserrated, with flutes and grooves; the formation was a mainly wetland environment of terrestrial and freshwater conditions.
author: Motta et al. 2026

sources.text: Matías J. Motta, Alexis M. Aranciaga Rolando, Sebastián Rozadilla, Federico L. Agnolín, Federico Brissón Egli, Gerardo P. Álvarez-Herrera, Nicolás R. Chimento, Gastón Lo Coco 2026. New unenlagiid from the Chorrillo Formation (Late Cretaceous, Maastrichtian), SW Patagonia, Argentina. Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology. doi:10.1080/02724634.2026.2656456

dates_note: No PBDB record. Chorrillo Formation is Maastrichtian (Wikipedia revision 1380974870); ICS bounds of the stage used.
